recommended_approach: Use a Mantaflow Liquid Domain workflow centered on Liquid domain settings with a FLIP-based simulation for splashy impact behavior, then tune particle controls (flip ratio, particle radius, sampling, randomness, min/max particles) to stabilize volume while preserving energetic splashes from the pour. Keep APIC as a fallback if FLIP becomes too chaotic and you need more stable vortices.

key_parameters.simulation_method: FLIP (docs: produces very splashy simulation with many dispersed particles)
key_parameters.flip_ratio: 1.0 gives fully FLIP behavior (more chaotic splashes); lower values reduce turbulence for subtler/smaller-scale motion
key_parameters.particle_radius: Increase if liquid appears to disappear/leak volume; decrease if too much liquid is produced
key_parameters.sampling_factor: Higher values sample more particles each simulation step
key_parameters.inflow_randomness: 0.0 gives uniform/laminar inflow; higher values add more turbulent/random inflow sampling
key_parameters.particles_max_per_cell: Use as upper resampling threshold to control particle count
key_parameters.particles_min_per_cell: Use to enforce minimum particle density per cell
key_parameters.viscosity_kinematic_reference: Water example from docs: ~1.002e-6 m^2/s (use diffusion/viscosity controls as physical baseline)
key_parameters.surface_tension: Use liquid diffusion surface tension controls to shape cohesion/splash breakup

warnings: Disabling the Liquid checkbox deletes the attached particle system and its settings.
A fully FLIP setup (flip ratio near 1.0) can become very chaotic; reduce ratio for less turbulent behavior if needed.
Volume-based emission requires a manifold/watertight mesh; certain modifiers can break watertightness.

alternative_approaches: Switch simulation method to APIC for more stable, energetic motion with better vortex preservation when FLIP is too chaotic.
Use lower FLIP contribution (flip ratio below full FLIP) to keep splash motion but reduce instability on small-scale glass shots.
